quizzes.title: Delimitation and the Commission: Practice Quiz
quizzes.passage: Delimitation is the process of drawing the boundaries of territorial constituencies so that representation stays fair as population changes. Over time, some constituencies grow much larger than others, which means that a vote in one area can carry less weight than a vote in another. For this reason, boundaries are not drawn once and left alone. Each redrawing exercise is carried out by a body called a Delimitation Commission, which is set up for that purpose. Such Commissions have been created under several Acts passed over a period of decades. They have not been appointed after every census, and at certain points the seat allocation among States was frozen to protect States that had controlled their population growth. Later changes to the Constitution continued these freezes. The same principle of fair representation also applies to the division of constituencies for State Assemblies, which follows its own constitutional provisions. Because the freeze was tied to population counts, the timing of the next redrawing has become a central question in the present debate over expanding the Lok Sabha. The question is not only how many seats exist but also how they are spread across regions. This makes the process both technical and politically sensitive, since every change in boundaries affects the candidates and voters in each area.

questions.q: Which Article governs the division of constituencies for State Assemblies?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that Article 170 governs the division of constituencies for State Assemblies.

questions.q: After which two Censuses was no Delimitation Commission formed?
questions.explanation: The booklet notes that no Commission was formed after the 1981 and 1991 Censuses.

questions.q: Which amendment extended the seat freeze until the first Census after 2026?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the 84th Amendment (2002) extended the freeze until the first Census after 2026.

questions.q:
Consider the following assertion and reason.
Assertion (A): The President appoints the Delimitation Commission in consultation with the Election Commission.
Reason (R): Article 82 requires Parliament to pass a Delimitation Act after every Census.
options: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: Both statements appear in the booklet, but the Article 82 requirement does not explain the consultation with the Election Commission.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Article 82
II. Article 170
III. 84th Amendment (2002)
IV. Appointment of the Delimitation Commission
A. Consultation with the Election Commission
B. Parliament to pass a Delimitation Act after every Census
C. Division of constituencies for State Assemblies
D. Extended the freeze until the first Census after 2026
questions.explanation: Article 82 matches the Delimitation Act requirement, Article 170 matches State Assembly constituencies, the 84th Amendment matches the extended freeze, and the appointment matches consultation with the Election Commission.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Delimitation Commission:
I. The Commission's functions include allocating seats among States.
II. Commissions have been formed under Acts of 1952, 1962 and 1972 only, with none under a later Act.
III. Rapid migration has overcrowded some urban constituencies.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are in the booklet, while II is contradicted by the 2002 Commission listed among the Acts.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about the Delimitation Commission are correct?
I. A Delimitation Commission was formed under an Act of 1972.
II. The Commission's decisions are final and not subject to modification by Parliament or State Assemblies.
III. A Delimitation Commission was formed after the 1981 Census.
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are supported by the booklet, while III contradicts its note that no Commission followed the 1981 Census.

questions.q: In which year was the most recent Delimitation Commission listed in the booklet formed under an Act? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Commissions formed under Acts of 1952, 1962, 1972 and 2002.

questions.q: Which body does the President consult before appointing the Delimitation Commission? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet states the President appoints the Commission in consultation with the Election Commission.

questions.q: Under which Article is the division of constituencies for State Assemblies governed? (Article number)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that Article 170 governs the division of constituencies for State Assemblies.

questions.q: Apart from a retired Supreme Court judge, which constitutional office holder is a member of the Delimitation Commission? (title)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists the Chief Election Commissioner and State Election Commissioners as Commission members.

questions.q: In which year was the earliest Delimitation Commission listed in the booklet formed? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Commissions formed under Acts of 1952, 1962, 1972 and 2002, so 1952 is the earliest.

questions.q: What quality is the Commission described as having, since it functions without executive influence? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes the Commission as functioning without executive influence, which is its independence.

questions.q: Apart from Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, for which group does the Commission decide reservations? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Commission decides reservations for SCs, STs and women.

quizzes.title: Concerns and Consequences: Practice Quiz
quizzes.passage: The proposed expansion of the Lok Sabha has been debated mainly for its effects on different parts of the country. Supporters of the change argue that a larger House would bring elected representatives closer to the people they serve, making it easier for citizens to raise their problems and seek a response. Critics reply that the benefits are not shared evenly, because the new seat arrangement would affect States differently depending on how their populations have grown over time. Some argue that the population figures used for the exercise may no longer match present conditions, and that the effects could last for many years. Others point to the design of the framework itself and ask how much room the rules leave for choices made at different stages. The discussion has also drawn in committees, public commentary and political parties, each setting out its own view of the reform. Taken together, these views show a debate about how representation, federal balance and effective governance should be weighed against one another. Each side supports its position with a different set of concerns about the design of the change and its likely results in the years ahead. Local perspectives on the issue also vary across regions, and this variation is part of why the debate remains open.

questions.q: What approximate share of Lok Sabha seats is the Southern States' share projected to fall to under the proposed delimitation?
questions.explanation: The booklet projects that the Southern States' share will fall from 24.3% to about 20.7%.

questions.q: Which chamber's federal role is said to be diluted by Lok Sabha dominance in joint sittings?
questions.explanation: In joint sittings, Lok Sabha dominance dilutes the Rajya Sabha's federal role.

questions.q: Which negative consequence is linked to Parliament's discretion over which population data to use?
questions.explanation: The booklet says Parliament's discretion may politicise delimitation.

questions.q:
Consider the following assertion and reason.
Assertion (A): Gerrymandering is identified as a risk in the proposed framework.
Reason (R): Judicial review of the delimitation process has been removed, leaving no court challenge.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The booklet links the gerrymandering risk directly to the removal of judicial review and the absence of court challenge.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Decline in legislative deliberation
II. Fiscal federal concerns
III. Better local development targeting
IV. Improved parliamentary functioning
A. Committee specialisation and policy expertise
B. Reduced speaking time per MP and weaker Question Hour scrutiny
C. Political weight may influence Finance Commission allocations
D. MPs handle smaller constituencies and make more efficient use of their development funds
questions.explanation: Each List I concern matches its consequence in List II as the booklet describes it.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the proposed Lok Sabha changes:
I. Smaller constituencies may improve grievance redressal.
II. Joint sittings are said to strengthen the Rajya Sabha's federal role.
III. Expansion may inflate the size of the Executive.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III reflect the booklet, whereas II reverses its point that joint sittings dilute the Rajya Sabha's role.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about the proposed Lok Sabha changes are correct?
I. Economically efficient but less populous States may be disadvantaged in Finance Commission allocations.
II. Census dependency is one reason women's reservation has been delayed.
III. Expansion increases the average size of constituencies.
questions.explanation: Statements I and II reflect the booklet, while III contradicts its point that expansion reduces constituency size.

questions.q: Removing judicial review is said to carry a risk of which practice? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists judicial review removed as carrying the risk of gerrymandering.

questions.q: Population-based delimitation is said to violate which principle of federalism? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet says population-based delimitation violates the spirit of cooperative federalism.

questions.q: Census dependency is cited as a reason for delay in implementing which reservation? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Census dependency among the reasons implementation of women's reservation is delayed.

questions.q: Political weight tied to population may influence allocations by which Commission? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet says political weight tied to population may influence Finance Commission allocations.

questions.q: Which constitutional amendment is cited as being supported by the expansion? (number)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the expansion facilitates women's reservation by supporting the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act 2023.

questions.q: In joint sittings, the dominance of the Lok Sabha dilutes the federal role of which chamber? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that in joint sittings Lok Sabha dominance dilutes the Rajya Sabha's federal role.
